name: Transfection Setup Calculator
seoDesc: Transfection protocols are written per well or per flask, and scaling them by hand is where experiments go wrong. Free transfection setup calculator: enter yo
summary:
Transfection protocols are written per well or per flask, and scaling them by hand is where experiments go wrong. It returns DNA per batch to make, reagent for the batch, diluent for the batch and total complex volume, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator scales DNA, transfection reagent and diluent from your reference format to the plate you actually have, with the complex formation time. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Transfection Setup
sections.html:
Scale factor = wells × 1.1 for pipetting loss; every component is multiplied by that factor, and the complex is formed at the reference ratio

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
DNAplasmid per wellµg
reagentlipid or polymer per wellµL
diluentserum-free medium per wellµL

sections.title: How do I use the Transfection Setup?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: dna in the reference well of 0.5 µg, reagent in the reference well of 1.5 µL, diluent per reference well of 50 µL, wells (or vessels) needed of 24.

Substituting them into the formula gives dna per batch to make of 13.2 µg, reagent for the batch of 39.6 µL, diluent for the batch of 1,320 µL, total complex volume of 1,359.6 µL, volume of complex per well of 51.5 µL.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
1:2 – 1:3DNA to reagenttypical for Lipofectamine-class reagents
15 – 30 minComplex formationroom temperature, no serum, no antibiotics
4 – 6 hExposurethen change to complete medium for sensitive cells

  • Make the DNA and the reagent dilutions in separate tubes before mixing; adding lipid straight onto DNA creates local excess and uneven complexes.

  • The 10% excess is not laziness: 24 wells need 25 wells' worth because no pipette delivers exactly what it draws.

  • Scale by surface area, not by well number, when moving between plate formats — a 6-well well holds ten times the area of a 96-well well.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Scaling a 24-well protocol to a 6-well plate by well count only.
  • Leaving complexes on the cells overnight, which is toxic for most primary cells.
  • Using medium with antibiotics during complex formation.

faq.q: How much DNA for a 6-well transfection?
faq.a: About 1–2 µg per well for a 9.6 cm² surface, roughly double a 12-well well.

faq.q: Can I scale this to a flask?
faq.a: Yes, but scale on growth area: a T-75 flask is about 8 times a 6-well well.

faq.q: What does the Transfection Setup actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns DNA per batch to make, reagent for the batch, diluent for the batch and total complex volume. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
